newsitem.title: USA: Iomega volume soars, tops Nasdaq actives.
newsitem.headline: Iomega volume soars, tops Nasdaq actives.

text.p: Shares of popular removable storage drive maker Iomega Corp again topped the Nasdaq most actives list, ending down 1-3/4 at 22-3/8 in volume of nearly 28 million shares.
Earlier in the session, the shares had risen as high as 27 in active trading, accounting for more than twice the volume of the next most heavily-traded Nasdaq stock.
Traders and analysts said the share's recent rise was connected to strength in the technology sector and to continuing deals with computer makers.
Last week, Iomega said Canon Inc's computer systems unit plans to incorporate its 100-megabyte Zip Drive as a standard feature in two Canon multimedia home PC models.

A week earlier, Iomega said it had agreed to grant Matsushita Communication Industrial Co's Matsushita Communication Industrial Co Ltd a nonexclusive worldwide licence to produce and to sell Zip drive compatible devices.

"I think a large part is the strength in the techs," said one analyst. "I think the stock was oversold, trading where it was at 12-13-14-15. They had some positive announcements about getting additional OEMs (computer makers)."

The stock had risen as high as 55-1/2 earlier in the year, boosted in part by main street investors enthusiastic over use of its relatively affordable, high density drives for backup storage and other purposes.
Iomega's volume of 27,819,600 was its seventh-highest volume since May 1995 and represented more than a fifth of the 136,257,126 shares it had outstanding as of August 1.
The Roy, Utah company issued no news and a spokesman was not immediately available.

But one of the small number of investment firms that cover Iomega, Emerald Research of Lancaster, Pa., said Iomega would make a presentation at an investment conference in Pittsburgh, Pa., on October 3.
Emerald analyst Joe Besecker was not immediately available for comment.
